newsitem.title: GERMANY: German institute sees 2.5 pct GDP growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: German institute sees 2.5 pct GDP growth in 1997.

text.p: Germany's Kiel Institute for Global Economics on Tuesday predicted that Germany's economic growth would accelerate in 1997 amid a recovery both at home and on the export side.
The institute predicted 2.5 percent growth in German gross domestic product in 1997 after 1.6 percent growth this year.
Domestic demand would improve significantly although growth in the eastern states, which has slowed considerably, would only marginally outstrip the western states, the institute predicted.
Low output in the East German construction sector would hamper developments in the region and the competitive position of the manufacturing sector would remain inadequate.
However continued strong growth in export demand would drive the overall recovery, helped by the mark's slight decline against the dollar, the institute predicted.
The dollar's gains against other currencies would continue in the coming year.
The institute also said the Bundesbank was unlikely to make any changes on interest rates for the time being.
While the central bank was unlikely to lower interest rates again, an interest rate hike was also unlikely before the end of 1997, given current low inflation rates.
